Hello! Good plan: these four words are very useful when you talk about your daily routine.

Our goal today is to describe a routine with always, usually, sometimes and never.

Imagine you are telling a new classmate about a normal week in your life. To start, write two sentences about yourself: one about something you do very often, and one about something you do not do at all. Use the four words if you can.
s2004_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NONE]]
Hello! Going to is a good topic for an exam, because we use it all the time to talk about plans.

Our goal today is to talk about plans with going to, and to say when they will happen.

Imagine a friend asks you, "What are your plans for the weekend?" To start, write one or two sentences that tell your friend about something you plan to do. Write it the way you would normally say it. We will look at it together next.
s2007_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NONE]]
Hello! Some and any are useful, and today's lesson is about ordering food and drink at a café. We will meet a/an and some there.

Our goal is to order politely and to choose the right small word before the thing you order.

Imagine you are at a café counter. The waiter looks at you and waits. To start, write what you would say to order one drink and one thing to eat. Write it the way you would normally say it.
s2010_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NONE]]
Hello! Polite requests are very common in exams and in real life, so this is a good choice.

Our goal today is to ask for something politely, with "Can I have ... please?", instead of a blunt command.

Imagine you are in a café and you are thirsty. The waiter comes to your table. To start, write exactly what you would say to ask for a glass of water. We will look at your sentence together next.

s2025_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: "an egg". Egg starts with a vowel sound, so we say an.
Rule: use a before a consonant sound, and an before a vowel sound.
Right: I see a cat. Wrong: I see an cat.
Your turn! Write a or an: I have ___ ant.
s2028_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: we take a bath in the bathroom.
Each place in a home has its job.
Right: We take a bath in the bathroom. Wrong: We take a bath in the garden.
Your turn! We play with a ball in the ___.
s2031_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: I see a bird. The bird is red.
Rule: say a the first time, then say the.
Right: I have a hat. The hat is red. Wrong: I have a hat. A hat is red.
Your turn! Write a or the: I see a cat. ___ cat is big.
s2034_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: I can clap.
Rule: after can, we use the plain verb, with no s.
Right: He can run. Wrong: He can runs.
Your turn! Finish the sentence: The cat can ___ (jump).
s2037_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: A nurse works in a hospital.
Rule: each job has its own place, and we say "works in" or "works at" with it.
Right: A teacher works in a school. Wrong: A teacher works in a hospital.
Your turn! Finish the sentence: A farmer works at a ___.
s2040_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: This is a pen.
Rule: say "This is a" and then the name of the thing.
Right: This is a book. Wrong: I hold a book and say, "This is a chair."
Your turn! I carry my books in it. This is a ___.
s2043_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Look: He jumps.
Rule: after he, she or it, we add -s to the verb.
Right: She cooks rice. Wrong: She cook rice.
Your turn! Write the verb with the right ending: The dog ___ (run) in the park.
s2046_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]

Rule: put the doer first, then the verb, then the object.
Right: Mia reads a book. Wrong: Reads Mia a book.
